anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Stale, missing, or insufficient statistics misrepresent real data distribution and lead the optimizer to misestimate cardinalities and costs.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: Even with acceptable statistics, the optimizer chooses or reuses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan because of cost-model bias, plan-cache effects, or version/configuration shifts.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: Network paths, listeners, authentication, or socket resources are saturated or unstable, delaying connection establishment and throttling data transfer between clients and the DBMS.

When all three root causes are present, database sessions experience extreme and erratic latency. Misestimated cardinalities steer the optimizer toward plans that are already poor; subsequent plan-selection pathologies (e.g., bad plan reuse, loss of parallelism) can further inflate execution time and I/O. The prolonged queries hold server back-end processes and large result sets open, which, combined with limited network throughput or frequent retransmissions, keeps sockets busy, inflates client-read waits, and exhausts connection pools. Symptoms include: dramatic swings between very fast and very slow runtimes for the same statements, execution plans whose estimates diverge wildly from actual rows, sudden shifts to full scans or nested-loop explosions, spikes in network wait events and TCP retransmits, growth of half-open or idle-in-transaction connections, application-side timeouts, and bursts of session reconnect attempts that hit listener backlog limits.

Causally, outdated or low-quality statistics are the first domino, skewing cost calculations. The optimizer may then lock in a flawed plan or reuse one unsuitable for current data, multiplying resource consumption. The heavier CPU, memory, and I/O load lengthens query and fetch phases, causing result sets to dribble over congested or lossy networks. Extended response times keep connections open longer, pushing the network layer toward saturation; conversely, network stalls can trigger query cancellations and forced recompilations, increasing plan churn and making statistic-driven misestimates more frequent. The positive feedback between bad plans and network contention amplifies both bottlenecks, degrading overall throughput and stability across OLTP and analytical workloads.

entry.official_description: Error when trying to fetch information from security context object, when trying to connect the server.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with connection establishment, authentication exchange, protocol correctness, network reachability, or client/server communication stability.
entry.solution_guidance: Check endpoint reachability, authentication flow, connection limits, protocol compatibility, transport stability, and client connection lifecycle management.
